# Ensemble Learning and Random Forests

**Estimated time: 1.5 hours**

Read **Chapter 7: Ensemble Learning and Random Forests**, from the beginning of the chapter **up to, but not including, Boosting**.

In the course edition, this corresponds approximately to **pp. 211–222**.

This reading introduces the broader idea of ensemble learning before focusing on random forests. The central idea is that combining multiple models can produce a more reliable predictor than relying on a single model.

Focus especially on:

- the idea of ensemble learning;
- how multiple decision trees can be combined;
- why random forests are more stable than individual decision trees;
- the important hyperparameters of a random forest.

## First Pass: Get the Big Picture — 10 minutes

- Skim the section titles.
- Look at the plots and figures.
- Read exercise questions 1–5.

## Second Pass: Read for Understanding — 60 minutes

Read from the beginning of Chapter 7 until the Boosting section.

Focus on understanding why combining multiple models works and how random forests introduce randomness across trees.

## Third Pass: Review — 20 minutes

Answer exercise questions 1–5.

Use the chapter to check and refine your answers.
